sanskrit: ṛṣer vacanam ājñāya rāmaḥ saṃdhyām upāsitum upākrāmat saraḥ puṇyam apsarobhir niṣevitam
english: Heeding the sage's word, Rāma set out to perform the twilight rite at the sacred lake frequented by the apsarases.

sanskrit: tatrodakam upaspṛṣśya saṃdhyām anvāsya paścimām āśramaṃ prāviśad rāmaḥ kumbhayoner mahātmanaḥ
english: Having touched the water there and performed the evening twilight observance, Rāma entered the hermitage of the great-souled Kumbhayoni — Agastya, born of a jar.

sanskrit: asyāgastyo bahuguṇaṃ phalamūlaṃ tathauṣadhīḥ śākāni ca pavitrāṇi bhojanārtham akalpayat
english: For him Agastya prepared abundantly rich fruits, roots, medicinal herbs, and pure pot-herbs for the evening meal.

sanskrit: sa bhuktavān naraśreṣṭhas tad annam amṛtopamam prītaś ca parituṣṭaś ca tāṃ rātriṃ samupāvasat
english: That foremost of men ate of that food resembling nectar, and, gratified and fully content, spent that night there.

sanskrit: prabhāte kālyam utthāya kṛtvāhnikam ariṃdamaḥ ṛṣiṃ samabhicakrāma gamanāya raghūttamaḥ
english: Rising early at dawn, having performed his daily morning duties, the best of the Raghu line — the subduer of foes — approached the sage to take his leave.

sanskrit: abhivādyābravīd rāmo maharṣiṃ kumbhasaṃbhavam āpṛcche tvāṃ gamiṣyāmi mām anujñātum arhasi
english: Saluting the great sage born of the kumbha — the jar — Rāma said: "I take my leave of you; I shall depart. Be pleased to give me your permission."

sanskrit: dhanyo 'smy anugṛhīto 'smi darśanena mahātmanaḥ draṣṭuṃ caivāgamiṣyāmi pāvanārtham ihātmanaḥ
english: "I am blessed, I have been favoured by the sight of the great-souled one. And I shall come here again to behold you, for the purification of my own self."

sanskrit: tathā vadati kākutsthe vākyam adbhutadarśanam uvāca paramaprīto dharmanetras tapodhanaḥ
english: As the descendant of Kākutstha spoke these words, wondrous to behold, the sage rich in austerities, whose eye is dharma, answered in utmost delight:

sanskrit: atyadbhutam idaṃ vākyaṃ tava rāma śubhākṣaram pāvanaḥ sarvalokānāṃ tvam eva raghunandana
english: "This speech of yours, O Rāma, is altogether wonderful, auspicious in every syllable. You yourself, O joy of the Raghu line, are the purifier of all worlds."

sanskrit: muhūrtam api rāma tvāṃ ye nu paśyanti ke cana pāvitāḥ svargabhūtās te pūjyante divi daivataiḥ
english: "Those beings who behold you even for a single moment, O Rāma, are purified and become as heaven itself; they are worshipped by the gods in the celestial realm."

sanskrit: ye ca tvāṃ ghoracakṣurbhir īkṣante prāṇino bhuvi hatās te yamadaṇḍena sadyo nirayagāminaḥ
english: "But those living beings on earth who gaze upon you with hostile eyes are struck down forthwith by the rod of Yama and go directly to hell."

sanskrit: gaccha cāriṣṭam avyagraḥ panthānam akutobhayam praśādhi rājyaṃ dharmeṇa gatir hi jagato bhavān
english: "Go then, untroubled, upon a path free from all peril. Rule your kingdom by dharma, for you are the very refuge of the world."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu muninā prāñjaliḥ prpagraho nṛpaḥ abhyavādayata prājñas tam ṛṣiṃ puṇyaśīlinam
english: Thus addressed by the sage, the wise king, composed and with palms joined in reverence, paid obeisance to that sage of holy conduct.

sanskrit: abhivādya muniśreṣṭhaṃ tāṃś ca sarvāṃs tapodhanān adhyārohat tad avyagraḥ puṣpakaṃ hemabhūṣitam
english: After reverencing the foremost among sages and all those who were rich in austerities, the unperturbed hero ascended that Puṣpaka chariot adorned with gold.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntaṃ munigaṇā āśīrvādaiḥ samantataḥ apūjayan mahendrābhaṃ sahasrākṣam ivāmarāḥ
english: As he departed, the hosts of sages honoured him on all sides with blessings, as the immortals honour thousand-eyed Indra blazing like Mahendra.

sanskrit: svasthaḥ sa dadṛśe rāmaḥ puṣpake hemabhūṣite śaśī meghasamīpastho yathā jaladharāgame
english: Serene, Rāma was a sight to behold upon the gold-adorned Puṣpaka, like the moon stationed near a cloud in the season of rain.

sanskrit: tato 'rdhadivase prāpte pūjyamānas tatas tataḥ ayodhyāṃ prāpya kākutstho vimānād avarohata
english: Then, when midday had arrived, honoured from every quarter, the descendant of Kākutstha reached Ayodhyā and descended from the aerial car.

sanskrit: tato visṛjya ruciraṃ puṣpakaṃ kāmagāminam kakṣyāntaravinikṣiptaṃ dvāḥsthaṃ rāmo 'bravīd vacaḥ
english: Then, having dismissed the beautiful Puṣpaka that travels at will, Rāma addressed a doorkeeper stationed in the inner courtyard:

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaṃ bharataṃ caiva gatvā tau laghuvikramau mamāgamanam ākhyāya śabdāpaya ca māṃ ciram
english: "Go to Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata — both of swift step — inform them of my arrival and then announce me for a long while."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā bhāṣitaṃ tasya rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ dvāḥsthaḥ kumārāv āhūya rāghavāya nyavedayat
english: Hearing that speech of Rāma — whose deeds cause no affliction — the doorkeeper summoned the two princes and reported it to the descendant of Raghu.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu rāghavaḥ prāptau priyau bharatalakṣmaṇau pariṣvajya tato rāmo vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Seeing the beloved Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa arrive, the descendant of Raghu — Rāma — embraced them and then spoke these words:

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ mayā yathātathyaṃ dvijakāryam anuttamam dharmasetumato bhūyaḥ kartum icchāmi rāghavau
english: "I have duly performed the most excellent duty owed to the twice-born; yet I wish to build the bridge of dharma still further, O descendants of Raghu."

sanskrit: yuvābhyām ātmabhūtābhyāṃ rājasūyam anuttamam sahito yaṣṭum icchāmi tatra dharmo hi śāśvataḥ
english: "Together with you two, who are as my own selves, I desire to perform the most excellent Rājasūya sacrifice — for therein eternal dharma resides."

sanskrit: iṣṭvā tu rājasūyena mitraḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ suhutena suyajñena varuṇatvam upāgamat
english: "Mitra, the destroyer of foes, having sacrificed at the Rājasūya with well-offered oblations and a well-conducted rite, attained the sovereignty of Varuṇa."

sanskrit: somaś ca rājasūyena iṣṭvā dharmeṇa dharmavit prāptaś ca sarvalokānāṃ kīrtiṃ sthānaṃ ca śāśvatam
english: "And Soma too, knower of dharma, having sacrificed rightly by the Rājasūya, attained everlasting glory among all worlds and an eternal station."

sanskrit: asminn ahani yac chreyaś cintyatāṃ tan mayā saha hitaṃ cāyati yuktaṃ ca prayatau vaktum arhatha
english: "Whatever is most beneficial on this day — let it be deliberated together with me; what is wholesome, what is fitting — you should speak freely, with care."

sanskrit: śrutā tu rāghavasyaitad vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ bharataḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Having heard these words of the descendant of Raghu, Bharata — skilled in the art of speech — joined his palms together and spoke these words:

sanskrit: tvayi dharmaḥ paraḥ sādho tvayi sarvā vasuṃdharā pratiṣṭhitā mahābāho yaśaś cāmitavikrama
english: "In you, O virtuous one, dharma supreme resides; in you the entire earth is established, O mighty-armed one; and in you rests glory, O you of immeasurable valour."

sanskrit: mahīpālāś ca sarve tvāṃ prajāpatim ivāmarāḥ nirīkṣante mahātmāno lokanāthaṃ yathā vayam
english: "All the great-souled guardians of the earth look to you as the immortals look to Prajāpati — as the lord of worlds — just as we do."

sanskrit: prajāś ca pitṛvad rājan paśyanti tvāṃ mahābala pṛthivyāṃ gatibhūto 'si prāṇinām api rāghava
english: "And the subjects regard you as a father, O great-powered king; you are the refuge on this earth for all living beings, O descendant of Raghu."

sanskrit: sa tvam evaṃvidhaṃ yajñam āhartāsi kathaṃ nṛpa pṛthivyāṃ rājavaṃśānāṃ vināśo yatra dṛśyate
english: "How can you, O king, perform such a sacrifice in which the destruction of royal lineages throughout the earth is foreseen?"

sanskrit: pṛthivyāṃ ye ca puruṣā rājan pauruṣam āgatāḥ sarveṣāṃ bhavitā tatra kṣayaḥ sarvāntakopamaḥ
english: "Those men of prowess upon the earth, O king — for all of them there will be destruction there, like the universal dissolution at the end of all things."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ puruṣaśārdūla guṇair atulavikrama pṛthivīṃ nārhase hantuṃ vaśe hi tava vartate
english: "You, O tiger among men, of matchless valour and virtue — you should not destroy the earth, for it stands already under your sway."

sanskrit: bharatasya tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvāmṛtamayaṃ yathā praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ
english: Hearing those words of Bharata, sweet as nectar, Rāma of true valour was filled with incomparable joy.

sanskrit: uvāca ca śubhāṃ vāṇīṃ kaikeyyā nandivardhanam prīto 'smi parituṣṭo 'smi tavādya vacanena hi
english: And he spoke an auspicious word to the one who increased Kaikeyī's delight: "I am pleased, I am fully content by your speech today."

sanskrit: idaṃ vacanam aklībaṃ tvayā dharmasamāhitam vyāhṛtaṃ puruṣavyāghra pṛthivyāḥ paripālanam
english: "This word spoken by you, O tiger among men, is without feebleness, grounded in dharma, and is truly the protection of the earth."

sanskrit: eṣa tasmād abhiprāyād rājasūyāt kratūttamān nivartayāmi dharmajña tava suvyāhṛtena vai
english: "From that intention, O knower of dharma, I now desist from the Rājasūya, that best of sacrifices, indeed by virtue of your well-spoken words."

sanskrit: prajānāṃ pālanaṃ dharmo rājñāṃ yajñena saṃmitaḥ tasmāc chṛṇomi te vākyaṃ sādhūktaṃ susamāhitam
english: "The protection of subjects is the dharma of kings, equal in worth to sacrifice. Therefore I heed your word, well and wisely spoken."

sanskrit: tathoktavati rāme tu bharate ca mahātmani lakṣmaṇo 'pi śubhaṃ vākyam uvāca raghunandanam
english: While Rāma was speaking thus and Bharata, the great-souled one, had spoken, Lakṣmaṇa too spoke an auspicious word to the joy of the Raghu line:

sanskrit: aśvamedho mahāyajñaḥ pāvanaḥ sarvapāpmanām pāvanas tava durdharṣo rocatāṃ kratupuṃgavaḥ
english: "The Aśvamedha — the great sacrifice, purifier of all sins — let that foremost of rites find favour with you, O invincible one; it shall purify you too."

sanskrit: śrūyate hi purāvṛttaṃ vāsave sumahātmani brahmahatyāvṛtaḥ śakro hayamedhena pāvitaḥ
english: "For it is heard in the tradition of former times that the great-souled Vāsava — Śakra — when enveloped by the sin of brahmanicide, was purified by the Aśvamedha."

sanskrit: purā kila mahābāho devāsurasamāgame vṛtro nāma mahān āsīd daiteyo lokasaṃmataḥ
english: "In ancient times, O mighty-armed one, there was in the great gathering of gods and asuras a great Daitya named Vṛtra, revered by all the worlds."

sanskrit: vistīrṇā yojanaśatam ucchritas triguṇaṃ tataḥ anurāgeṇa lokāṃs trīn snehāt paśyati sarvataḥ
english: "A hundred yojanas in breadth and three times that in height, he regarded the three worlds with affection and looked upon all with tender love."

sanskrit: dharmajñaś ca kṛtajñaś ca buddhyā ca pariniṣṭhitaḥ śaśāsa pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ dharmeṇa susamāhitaḥ
english: "Knowing dharma and knowing gratitude, perfected in intellect, he ruled all the earth steadily by dharma."

sanskrit: tasmin praśāsati tadā sarvakāmadughā mahī rasavanti prasūtāni mūlāni ca phalāni ca
english: "While he was reigning, the earth yielded all desires; roots and fruits were produced full of nourishment."

sanskrit: akṛṣṭapacyā pṛthivī susaṃpannā mahātmanaḥ sa rājyaṃ tādṛśaṃ bhuṅkte sphītam adbhutadarśanam
english: "The earth ripened without tilling, abundantly rich; that great-souled one enjoyed a kingdom so prosperous and wondrous to behold."

sanskrit: tasya buddhiḥ samutpannā tapaḥ kuryām anuttamam tapo hi paramaṃ śreyas tapo hi paramaṃ sukham
english: "Then a resolve arose in his mind: I shall practise the most excellent austerity, for austerity is the highest good, austerity is the highest bliss."

sanskrit: sa nikṣipya sutaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ paureṣu parameśvaram tapa ugram upātiṣṭhat tāpayan sarvadevatāḥ
english: "Entrusting his eldest son as supreme lord over the citizens, he undertook fierce austerity, scorching all the gods with its heat."

sanskrit: tapas tapyati vṛtre tu vāsavaḥ paramārtavat viṣṇuṃ samupasaṃkramya vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: "While Vṛtra was performing austerities, Vāsava, exceedingly troubled, approached Viṣṇu and spoke these words:"

sanskrit: tapasyatā mahābāho lokā vṛtreṇa nirjitāḥ balavān sa hi dharmātmā nainaṃ śakṣyāmi bādhitum
english: "'By his austerities, O mighty-armed one, the worlds have been conquered by Vṛtra; he is powerful and virtuous in soul — I am not able to vanquish him."

sanskrit: yady asau tapa ātiṣṭhed bhūya eva sureśvara yāval lokā dhariṣyanti tāvad asya vaśānugāḥ
english: "'If he continues his austerities still further, O lord of gods, then as long as the worlds endure they will be subject to his sway."

sanskrit: tvaṃ cainaṃ paramodāram upekṣasi mahābala kṣaṇaṃ hi na bhaved vṛtraḥ kruddhe tvayi sureśvara
english: "'And you, of immense power, hold this most magnanimous one in disregard — yet Vṛtra would not last even a moment were you wrathful, O lord of gods."

sanskrit: yadā hi prītisaṃyogaṃ tvayā viṣṇo samāgataḥ tadā prabhṛti lokānāṃ nāthatvam upalabdhavān
english: "'For ever since I entered into the bond of friendship with you, O Viṣṇu, I have obtained from that time forward the lordship over all the worlds."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ prasādaṃ lokānāṃ kuruṣva sumahāyaśaḥ tvatkṛtena hi sarvaṃ syāt praśāntam ajaraṃ jagat
english: "'You then, O one of surpassing glory, extend your grace to the worlds; for by your action the entire universe would become at peace and free from decay."

sanskrit: ime hi sarve viṣṇo tvāṃ nirīkṣante divaukasaḥ vṛtraghatena mahatā eṣāṃ sāhyaṃ kuruṣva ha
english: "'All these dwellers in heaven look to you, O Viṣṇu; by the great slaying of Vṛtra render them your aid."

sanskrit: tvayā hi nityaśaḥ sāhyaṃ kṛtam eṣāṃ mahātmanām asahyam idam anyeṣām agatīnāṃ gatir bhavān
english: "'For you have always rendered aid to these great-souled ones; this burden is unbearable for others — you are the refuge of those who have no other refuge.'"
